findings.summary: The .cfg visual editor's header row is built from TableBodyCell, which renders <td>, so the table has no <th>: Property / Key, Value and Security are not associated with the cells or controls below them.
findings.fix: Use moonstone's TableHeadCell (renders <th>) or <TableBodyCell component="th" scope="col"> for every cell of CfgEditorHeader, with scope="col".

findings.summary: The YAML visual editor's header row (Property / Key, Value, Security, Actions) uses TableBodyCell, i.e. <td>, so no cell has a column header.
findings.fix: Replace the four TableBodyCell in the <thead> with <TableHeadCell scope="col"> (or TableBodyCell component="th" scope="col"), keeping the sticky styles.

findings.summary: Three columns of the .cfg table (reorder handle, entry type, delete action at lines 181, 182, 202) have empty header cells, so their content has no header once headers become <th>.
findings.fix: Give each header a visually hidden text: e.g. {t('editor.header.order')}, ...{t('editor.header.type')}..., and {t('editor.header.actions')} (key already exists in en.json). Add the new keys to every locale file.

findings.summary: The .cfg properties table has no <caption>, aria-label or aria-labelledby, so screen readers announce an unnamed table.
findings.fix: Name the table after the file: <Table aria-label={t('editor.table.label', {name: filename})}> or a visually hidden <caption> as the first child (CfgEditor needs the filename prop, available in index.jsx as selectedFile.name).

findings.summary: The YAML properties table has no <caption> or accessible name.
findings.fix: Add a visually hidden <caption> or aria-label naming the file, e.g. 'Properties of {{name}}', as for CfgEditor.

findings.summary: In the YAML table the property key cell identifies each row but is a <td>, so the Value, Security and Actions cells are not announced with their property name.
findings.fix: Render the key cell as <TableBodyCell component="th" scope="row">. Include the parent path in it as visually hidden text (see TREE-HIERARCHY) so a nested key is unambiguous.

findings.summary: The per-row encryption checkbox has no accessible name: moonstone's Checkbox renders a bare <input type="checkbox">, and the title on the parent <td> does not name it.
findings.fix: Pass a name with row context: <Checkbox aria-label={t('editor.encryptValueOf', {key})} .../> (e.g. 'Encrypt value of {{key}}'); add the key to every locale file.

findings.summary: In the YAML table the encryption checkbox (line 125) and the value editors shown on edit (MultilineInput line 87, Input line 93) have no accessible name.
findings.fix: Add aria-label with the property: Checkbox aria-label 'Encrypt value of {{key}}'; Input and textarea aria-label 'Value of {{key}}' (pass rowLabel or keyString into LeafRow's editors).

findings.summary: Row controls of the .cfg table carry the same name in every row: textareas named only by placeholders 'Key'/'Value', and 'Delete this property', 'Reorder this entry...', 'Show secret value' with no property name.
findings.fix: Include the key in each name: key textarea aria-label 'Key of row {{n}}', value aria-label 'Value of {{key}}', delete aria-label 'Delete {{key}}', reorder aria-label 'Reorder {{key}}...', secret toggle 'Show value of {{key}}'. Keep the visible text inside each aria-label (2.5.3).

findings.summary: moonstone TableRow renders <tr tabIndex=0> by default, so every row of the .cfg table, the YAML table (Editor.jsx:61, 160) and the file list (FileSidebar.jsx:137) is an extra Tab stop with no action of its own.
findings.fix: Pass tabIndex={-1} to TableRow in CfgEditor.jsx:583 and Editor.jsx:61/160 (rows stay clickable, Tab goes straight to the cell controls). In FileSidebar, replace the rows as per the file-list finding instead.
findings.evidence: moonstone 2.20.3 TableRow: z.createElement(t /* 'tr' */, { className: ..., tabIndex: 0, ...o, ref: s })

findings.summary: After Arrow Up/Down moves an entry, focus stays on the handle at the old index (rows are keyed by index, line 584), which now belongs to the neighbouring entry; a second key press moves the wrong row, and nothing announces the new position.
findings.fix: After handleReorder(index, target), focus the reorder button of row target (keep a ref map like inputRefs) and announce 'Moved {{key}} to position {{n}} of {{total}}' in a role="status" region. Also ignore the keys while filtering, as the drag handler does at line 600, since index±1 may be a hidden row.
findings.evidence: key={index} ... onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === 'ArrowUp' && index > 0) { e.preventDefault(); handleReorder(index, index - 1); } ... }}

findings.summary: Filtering the .cfg table updates a visible count 'Matching properties: N' that is not a status message, so screen reader users are not told how many rows remain, including when none match.
findings.fix: Render a container that always exists with role="status" (aria-live polite) and put the count text inside it only while filtering, so the update is announced.

findings.summary: YAML sections collapse through onClick on a <td> with chevron icons: not focusable, no button role, no aria-expanded, so keyboard and screen reader users cannot open or close a section or know its state.
findings.fix: Put a real button in the container cell: <button type="button" aria-expanded={!isCollapsed} onClick={toggleCollapse}>{chevron}{folder}{displayLabel}</button>, with the icons aria-hidden. Keep the Add Property button outside it.
findings.evidence: <TableBodyCell colSpan={4} style={{ ..., cursor: 'pointer' }} onClick={toggleCollapse}>{isCollapsed ? <ChevronRight size="small" /> : <ChevronDown size="small" />}

findings.summary: The nesting of YAML keys is shown only by left padding (level * 20px), a blue left border and backgrounds; a screen reader reads a flat list of rows where 'port' under two parents is indistinguishable.
findings.fix: Simplest: make the key cell a row header (th scope="row") holding a visually hidden parent path, e.g. 'server › http › ' before the key. Full option: role="treegrid" with aria-level, aria-expanded and aria-posinset/setsize, which also requires grid keyboard navigation; prefer the simple option.
findings.evidence: paddingLeft: `${level * 20 + 20}px` (LeafRow) / paddingLeft: `${level * 20 + 10}px`, borderLeft: level > 0 ? '4px solid #007cb0' : 'none' (ContainerRow, line 164)

findings.summary: A YAML value becomes editable only on double-click of a non-focusable div, so keyboard users cannot edit values in the visual editor (only the raw Monaco mode remains).
findings.fix: Make the value cell's trigger focusable: a <button type="button" aria-label={`Edit value of ${rowLabel}`}> that sets editingValueKey on click/Enter, or always render the Input. Return focus to that trigger when the editor blurs.
findings.evidence: <div onMouseEnter=... onDoubleClick={() => { onHideOverlay(); setEditingValueKey(keyString); }} style={{ cursor: 'text', ... }}>

findings.summary: When a file has no entries (or every row is hidden by filter or comment toggles) the .cfg and YAML tables (Editor.jsx:334) render only their header row, with no message.
findings.fix: When no row renders, add <TableRow><TableBodyCell colSpan={6}>{t('editor.noEntries')}</TableBodyCell></TableRow> (colSpan={4} in Editor.jsx), with a filter-specific text when filtering.

findings.summary: The file list is a one-dimensional list drawn as a two-column <table> with no headers or caption; the first column holds only a colour bar, so table navigation adds noise and Chromium may expose it as a layout table.
findings.fix: Use list or listbox semantics instead of a table (see link-checker LINK-CONTROL-ELEMENT at FileSidebar.jsx:137): <ul aria-label={t('app.fileListLabel')}> with one item per file, or role="listbox". 1.3.1 does not require table semantics here.

findings.summary: Each file's enabled/disabled status is shown only by a 3px green/grey bar and a line-through (line 173), and its origin (module, module default, user) only by an unlabelled icon chip (line 176) whose tooltip needs hover.
findings.fix: Add text for each state to every file item: visually hidden ', disabled' when !f.enabled, and the state label (t(config.labelKey)) as visually hidden text next to the compact chip, or aria-describedby. Keep the bar and the chip as decoration (aria-hidden).

findings.summary: The review diff marks added and removed lines only by background and text colour on <span>s, with no +/- marker, <ins>/<del> or text, so screen reader users and users who cannot tell red from green cannot see which lines change.
findings.fix: Render added parts as <ins> and removed parts as <del>, each starting with visually hidden 'Added:' / 'Removed:' text (screen readers often ignore ins/del by default), plus a visible +/- gutter for 1.4.1. Table semantics are not needed: the unified diff is a single column.
findings.evidence: <span key={index} style={{ backgroundColor: part.added ? '#e6ffec' : part.removed ? '#ffebe9' : 'transparent', color: part.added ? '#1e7e34' : part.removed ? '#cb2431' : '#333', display: 'block' }}>

findings.summary: The diff body is a scroll container (maxHeight 60vh, overflowY auto) with nothing focusable inside, so in browsers that do not make scrollers focusable, keyboard users cannot scroll a long diff.
findings.fix: Make the region focusable and named: tabIndex={0} role="region" aria-label={t('modal.diff.title', {name: filename})}, with a visible focus outline.

findings.summary: Collections of property and template cards are bare divs (here, CfgMetatypePropertyDialog.jsx:146 and Dialogs.jsx:369/409), so screen readers do not announce a list or the number of items.
findings.fix: Wrap each collection in <ul role="list"> with one <li> per card (role="list" keeps semantics when list-style is none in Safari), keeping the button or radio inside each item.

passed: The .cfg and YAML property lists are real tables (moonstone Table/TableBody/TableRow/TableBodyCell render <table>/<tbody>/<tr>/<td>), not div grids, so 1.3.1 does not require converting div layouts there.
No role="grid" or treegrid misuse, and no layout table needing role="presentation" (the file list is reported as a list drawn as a table).
colSpan values match the column count: CfgEditor comment row 1+1+2+1+1 = 6 columns (line 636), YAML container row colSpan=4 for 4 columns (Editor.jsx:162).
No sortable columns, pagination, select-all checkbox or row multi-selection, so aria-sort, aria-current pagination and indeterminate-state checks do not apply.
Drag reordering has a keyboard alternative (reorder button, CfgEditor.jsx:608-622), so it is not drag-only (2.5.7).
DiffModal: a unified single-column diff with no line numbers or side-by-side columns is not tabular data; 1.3.1 does not require table semantics, only change markers (reported separately).

Metatype metadata inside cards ('Type: x', 'Optional: yes', 'Default: y', MonacoEditor.jsx:1551-1567; CfgMetatypePropertyDialog.jsx:179-188) keeps the label in the same text as the value, so <dl> markup is not required.
Masked values in the YAML table show a text placeholder ('*****', Editor.jsx:120) rather than an empty cell.
notes: moonstone internals (TableRow defaults to tabIndex=0, TableBodyCell renders <td>, TableHeadCell renders <th>, Checkbox renders an unlabelled <input>) were read from @jahia/moonstone 2.20.3 in a sibling worktree; this worktree has no node_modules and package.json asks for ^2.21.0. Confirm in the browser that the behaviour did not change.

moonstone Table and TableRow add flex display classes (flexCol_nowrap, flexRow) to <table> and <tr>. Some browser/screen-reader pairs, notably WebKit with VoiceOver, have dropped table semantics when the display is overridden. Check the accessibility tree at the page URL (run_playwright_a11y_tree) for role table/row/columnheader after the <th> fix.

Decision for the team: for the YAML editor, a hidden parent path in a row header plus disclosure buttons (recommended) versus a full ARIA treegrid, which also requires arrow-key cell navigation and roving tabindex.

Overlap with other specialists: hover-only overflow previews (Editor.jsx:46, CfgEditor.jsx:313, AppChrome.jsx:163) and the hover-only metatype 'i' tooltip trigger (CfgEditor.jsx:696, a non-focusable div) fall under 1.4.13 / 2.1.1 and are left to the keyboard and ARIA specialists.
